title: Washington WR Christian Moss Sidelined 2 to 3 Months With Lower-Body Injury
dek: Washington wide receiver Christian Moss will miss two to three months with a lower-body injury sustained in the season opener against Washington State, per head coach Jedd Fisch. The loss compounds offensive depth issues for the Huskies heading into Big Ten play.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Moss, starting receiver for the Huskies and 2025 transfer with 65 career receptions, will be re-evaluated November 1.
bottom_line: The November 1 re-evaluation window for Moss, Carr, and Limar will fall near midseason, creating a six-week window for the Huskies to establish offensive consistency before these players potentially return. The depth of reserves at wide receiver and running back, alongside Williams's status, will determine how effectively Washington can absorb the concurrent losses.
body:
Washington wide receiver Christian Moss will miss two to three months with a lower-body injury, head coach Jedd Fisch announced on Monday, September 15, 2026. Moss sustained the injury in the Huskies' season opener against Washington State and did not record any statistics in that game.
Moss, a transfer from Kennesaw State, produced 45 receptions for 689 yards and two touchdowns last season. Across his college career at Kennesaw State and Virginia Tech, he holds 65 career receptions for 963 yards and four touchdowns. The re-evaluation date is set for November 1, placing his return during Big Ten conference play.
Moss's absence compounds an injury toll across Washington's offensive core. Starting running back Quaid Carr and backup running back Jayden Limar will both miss two to three months after being injured against Washington State. Quarterback Demond Williams Jr. has been the primary rusher, with reserve backs Trey Cooley and Brian Bonner Jr. each recording 22 yards in Washington's subsequent win over Utah State.
Fisch indicated Williams' potential absence would not be substantial.  Freshman defensive tackle Derek Colman-Brusa required stitches in his finger from a play in the Utah State game but is expected to be fine.
Washington will host Eastern Washington this week before opening Big Ten play at home against Minnesota on September 26, 2026.
